mainTopic: Testing the מחלוקת of אביי and רבא (does a forbidden act still take effect?) against the cases of אונס, תרומה, and חרמים
overview: Earlier in the סוגיא, אביי and רבא argued about an act the תורה forbids: if someone does it anyway, does it still work? אביי says it works. רבא says it does not, and the person still gets מלקות for breaking the תורה's word. The גמרא now tests both views on one case after another. First comes a ברייתא about an אונס who divorced his victim, which is used against רבא in one version and against אביי in another; both sides explain it with the words "כל ימיו". Next, תרומה from bad produce for good produce works even though it is forbidden, and רבא answers with רבי אילעא's פסוק about "bearing sin". Then תרומה from one type for another does not work, and אביי answers with the extra word "ראשית". Last, חרמים may not be redeemed and redemption fails, and אביי explains that "קדש קדשים הוא" means a חרם stays as it is. Each side keeps its general rule and treats the other side's cases as special exceptions taught by a פסוק.

steps.title: A rapist who divorced is not flogged: a challenge to רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that an ישראל אונס who divorced his victim takes her back and gets no מלקות. That seems to contradict רבא, who holds that breaking the תורה's word brings מלקות even if the act does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: A rapist who divorced his victim, if he is an Israelite, takes her back and is not flogged. But if you say that whoever transgresses the word of the Merciful One is flogged, this man should also be flogged! This is a refutation of רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רבא. The ברייתא says the divorcing אונס is not flogged, but רבא's rule seems to say he should be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids an אונס to ever send his victim away. He did send her away, so he broke the word of the תורה. By רבא's logic that alone should bring מלקות, yet the ברייתא says no מלקות, so this looks like a full refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who forced himself on a girl. The תורה obligates him to marry her and never divorce her.
He takes her back (remarries her).
He receives מלקות (lashes).
He transgressed the word of the Merciful One (the תורה).
A strong refutation that seems to knock down an opinion.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A rapist who divorced [his victim],
if he is an Israelite
he takes her back and is not flogged.
And if you say
that since he transgressed the word of the Merciful One he is flogged,
then this one should be flogged too!
A refutation of Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to רבא's position from the earlier part of the סוגיא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that anyone who transgresses the תורה's word is flogged.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אונס transgressed by divorcing, yet the ברייתא says he is not flogged, so רבא's rule seems wrong.

steps.title: רבא answers: "all his days" keeps the obligation open
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the אונס case is special. The פסוק says "כל ימיו", so his whole life he remains obligated to take her back. When he does take her back, he has not broken the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could say to you: It is different there, because the verse says "all his days." All his days he stands under the command to get up and take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself. He says the אונס case is an exception because of the special words "כל ימיו" in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition is only fully broken if he keeps her divorced for his whole life. Once he takes her back, it turns out he never truly violated it. So there is no reason for מלקות, and רבא's general rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there. This is a way of saying the case is an exception.
All his days. These are the words of the פסוק about the אונס.
Under the command to arise and take her back.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: a prohibition that can be fixed for the rest of one's life does not bring מלקות once it is fixed.

phrases.english: He [Rava] could say to you:
It is different there,
for the verse says "all his days,"
all his days he stands under "arise and take her back."
phrases.notes: He means the duty stays on him his whole life. So if he takes her back, he hasn't really broken it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תיובתא against רבא from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (שאני התם) based on a special word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The divorce is a completed sin, so רבא should require מלקות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of "כל ימיו", the sin is only complete if he never takes her back. Once he does, there is no violation and no מלקות.

steps.title: What אביי learns from "all his days"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what אביי, who does not need "כל ימיו" for רבא's point, learns from it. Without these words we might think the אונס may choose not to take her back. The words teach that he must take her back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי, what does "all his days" teach? If the Merciful One had not said "all his days," I would have said that he merely did a forbidden act, and if he wants he may take her back and if he wants he need not take her back. The verse teaches us that he must take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what "כל ימיו" teaches according to אביי, and answers right away. The words teach that the אונס is obligated to remarry her, not just allowed to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without these words, we would treat the divorce as a one-time sin that is already finished, so remarrying would be optional. "כל ימיו" shows that the obligation to be married to her continues, so he must take her back.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought. This is the mistaken first idea before the פסוק teaches otherwise.
A prohibition (a forbidden act).
It teaches us. This introduces the new point we learn.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי ignores "כל ימיו". Both agree the words are needed. They just learn different points from them.

phrases.english: And according to Abaye [what does "all his days" teach]?
If the Merciful One had not said "all his days,"
I would have said
that it is just a prohibition that he did,
if he wants, he may take her back,
and if he wants, he need not take her back;
so it teaches us [that he must take her back].

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַבָּיֵי, אִי לָאו דַּאֲמַר רַחֲמָנָא ״כׇּל יָמָיו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא used "כל ימיו" in step 2, the גמרא explains how אביי uses the same words.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It teaches that remarrying her is required, not optional.

steps.title: Another version: the same ברייתא challenges אביי
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of the discussion, the same ברייתא is quoted in full, including the case of a כהן. Its ruling that an ישראל takes her back is used as a תיובתא against אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: They challenged from a ברייתא: A rapist who divorced his victim, if he is an Israelite, takes her back and is not flogged. If he is a כהן, he is flogged and does not take her back. It teaches "if he is an Israelite he takes her back". This is a refutation of אביי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the discussion. This time the ברייתא is used to attack אביי instead of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says he must take her back, which suggests the forbidden divorce did not really work. That fits רבא and seems to go against אביי, who holds that forbidden acts do take effect. A כהן cannot take back a divorced woman, so he stays with his sin and gets מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of how the discussion went.
A כהן, who is forbidden to marry a divorced woman.

steps.whatToRemember: The same ברייתא about the אונס is used in one version against רבא and in another version against אביי. The words "כל ימיו" are central to the answer in both.

phrases.english: Another version.
They raised an objection: A rapist who divorced [his victim],

phrases.aramaic: אִם יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מַחְזִיר וְאֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה,
phrases.english: if he is an Israelite, he takes her back and is not flogged,
and if he is a priest,
he is flogged and does not take her back.
It teaches: "If he is an Israelite he takes her back"
A refutation of Abaye!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the discussion in a second version, now aimed at אביי instead of רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that a forbidden act still takes effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires the ישראל to take her back, which suggests the forbidden divorce did not take effect. That contradicts אביי.

steps.title: אביי answers that the אונס case is special
steps.stepSummary: אביי defends himself. The פסוק "כל ימיו" means the אונס is always obligated to take her back, so in this one case his divorce does not settle anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the תורה says "all his days." All his days he stays under the command to get up and take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the תיובתא from step 4. He says the אונס is a special case because of the words "כל ימיו".
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי normally holds that a forbidden act still works. The ברייתא says the ישראל takes her back, which looks like his divorce did not work. אביי explains that "כל ימיו" makes this case an exception: the obligation to take her back never ends, so his general rule is not disproved.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there. Used to show a case is an exception.
All his days. The words of the פסוק about the אונס.
Get up and take her back. The ongoing obligation of the אונס.

phrases.english: It is different there
for the Merciful One said: "all his days"
all his days he is under "get up and take her back."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תיובתא against אביי raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the proof to a special case based on a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that a forbidden divorce does not work, against אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the אונס is special, because "כל ימיו" keeps his obligation alive forever. אביי's general rule still stands.

steps.title: What רבא learns from "all his days"
steps.stepSummary: רבא does not need "כל ימיו" to show the act does not work, since he holds that anyway. For him, the words teach that the אונס gets no מלקות, because his prohibition is a לאו הניתק לעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא would tell you: if the תורה had not written "all his days," I would have said that he gets lashes and also takes her back, because it would be a plain prohibition, as it says "he may not send her away." That is why the פסוק wrote "all his days": to make the אונס a prohibition that is fixed by a positive command, and for that kind of prohibition one does not get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבא reads "כל ימיו", since in this version אביי used it for his own answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without "כל ימיו", "לא יוכל לשלחה" would be a plain לאו, and breaking it would bring מלקות. "כל ימיו" adds that he can always fix it by taking her back, so it becomes a לאו הניתק לעשה. That kind of לאו gets no מלקות, and this explains why the ברייתא says he is not lashed.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought. The mistaken first idea before the פסוק teaches otherwise.
A plain prohibition, with nothing attached to fix it.
A prohibition that is fixed by doing a positive command. One does not get lashes for it.
Lashes given by בית דין for breaking a לאו.

phrases.english: And רבא would say to you:
if the Merciful One had not written "all his days"
I would have said: let him be lashed and take her back
since it would be a plain prohibition
as it is written: "he may not send her away."
That is why the verse wrote "all his days"
to make the rapist's case
into a prohibition that is fixed by a positive command
for which one does not get lashes.

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, אביי uses "כל ימיו" to explain why the divorce does not settle anything. רבא uses it to explain why there is no מלקות.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the other side, רבא, uses the same פסוק that אביי just used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבא learn from "כל ימיו", since he does not need it to show that the act does not work?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It makes the אונס's prohibition a לאו הניתק לעשה, so he gets no מלקות.

steps.title: A new case: separating תרומה from poor produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new case against רבא. Separating תרומה from bad produce for good produce is forbidden by a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the case of one who separates תרומה from bad produce for good produce, which is forbidden, since the תורה says "from all its best."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge to רבא. First it shows that this act is forbidden by the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To challenge רבא, the גמרא needs a case that is both forbidden and still effective. This line sets up the first half: the פסוק "מכל חלבו" forbids giving תרומה from poor produce. The next step will show that it still works.

keyTerms.meaning: One who separates תרומה, the portion given to a כהן.
From the bad produce for the good produce.
Its best part. Literally "its fat."

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי תּוֹרֵם מִן הָרָעָה עַל הַיָּפָה
phrases.english: But there is one who separates תרומה from bad produce for good produce
for the Merciful One said: "from all its best."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי תּוֹרֵם מִן הָרָעָה עַל הַיָּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אונס case and brings a new case to test רבא's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that whatever the תורה forbids does not work if done
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step shows the act is forbidden. The next step will show that it still works.

steps.title: The משנה says the forbidden תרומה still works
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק excludes poor produce, yet the משנה rules that if someone did give it, it is real תרומה. A forbidden act works, so this is a תיובתא against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Its best" - yes; poor produce - no. And we learned in a משנה: one may not separate תרומה from bad produce for good produce, but if he did, his תרומה is real תרומה. So it works. This is a refutation of רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. It brings a משנה showing that the forbidden תרומה still counts, and calls it a תיובתא against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says that anything the תורה forbids does not work if done. Here the תורה forbids poor-quality תרומה, but the משנה says it still becomes תרומה. That fits אביי and seems to refute רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Poor-quality produce.
It works, it takes effect.
So we see, apparently.
A strong refutation of an opinion.

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying the act is allowed. It says you may not do it, but if you did, it still counts. That gap between "forbidden" and "works" is the whole argument.

phrases.english: "Its best" - yes; poor produce - no.

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין מִן הָרָעָה עַל הַיָּפָה
phrases.english: And we learned: one may not separate תרומה from bad produce for good produce
but if he did separate, his תרומה is תרומה.
So we see it works
a refutation of רבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין מִן הָרָעָה עַל הַיָּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up in step 7 by showing the forbidden act still works.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a forbidden act does not work
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה forbids poor-quality תרומה, yet the משנה says it is valid תרומה. A forbidden act that works contradicts רבא.

steps.title: רבא explains why bad-for-good תרומה works
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the bad-produce case is special. A פסוק, explained by רבי אילעא, shows that this תרומה works even though the act is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא can answer: That case is different, because of what רבי אילעא taught. How do we know that if someone separates תרומה from bad produce for good produce, it counts as תרומה? Because the verse says, 'You will bear no sin because of it when you separate its best part.' If it did not become holy, why would there be any sin? So we learn that it does count as תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself against the challenge from step 8. He agrees the bad-produce case works, but says a special פסוק teaches that, so it does not disprove his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'bearing sin' when separating. רבי אילעא argues that you can only sin with תרומה if it actually became holy, so the פסוק itself shows it works. For רבא this is a special exception taught by the פסוק. His general rule, that a forbidden act does not work, stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; that case is special
Separating תרומה from bad produce to cover good produce
Bearing sin, being guilty of a wrong
Becomes holy; here, takes effect as real תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not admitting that forbidden acts work in general. He says only that this one case works, because the פסוק specially teaches it.

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:
It is different there, in line with Rabbi Ile'a,
as Rabbi Ile'a said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לְתוֹרֵם מִן הָרָעָה עַל הַיָּפָה
phrases.english: From where do we know that one who separates terumah from the bad produce for the good produce,
that his terumah is real terumah?
As it says: "And you shall bear no sin because of it
when you separate its best part from it."
If it does not become holy,
why would there be any sin?

phrases.aramaic: מִיכָּן לַתּוֹרֵם מִן הָרָעָה עַל הַיָּפָה
phrases.english: From here we learn that one who separates from the bad for the good,
his terumah is real terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תיובתא against רבא from step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bad-produce case seemed to prove that forbidden acts work in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only this case works, because the פסוק's mention of 'sin' shows the תרומה took effect.

steps.title: Why אביי still needs the verse about sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words 'you shall bear no sin' teach according to אביי. The answer: they teach that taking from bad produce is a real sin, not just a missed chance to do the best thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי, what does the verse teach? Without the words 'you will bear no sin,' I would have thought the תורה only meant: do the מצוה in the best way, but if you don't, you are not called a sinner. So the verse teaches us that it is a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: Since אביי already holds that forbidden acts work, he does not need the פסוק to show that the תרומה counts. The גמרא explains what the פסוק teaches him instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the פסוק is not needed to show the תרומה works. Instead, it tells us that giving from bad produce is a real wrongdoing. Without it, we might have thought giving from the best produce was only extra credit.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing a מצוה in the best possible way
A sinner
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
It teaches us (the new point the source adds)

phrases.english: And according to Abaye, [why is this verse needed?]
If the Merciful One had not said
"And you shall bear no sin because of it,"
I would have thought that this is what the Merciful One said:
Do the מצוה in the best way,
but if he did not do it that way,
he is not called a "sinner."
So the verse teaches us [that he is a sinner].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 9 used the פסוק for רבא; this step shows how אביי reads the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'you shall bear no sin' teach according to אביי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It teaches that giving תרומה from bad produce is a real sin, not just a failure to do the מצוה in the best way.

steps.title: Challenge to אביי: תרומה from a different type of produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new case against אביי. The תורה requires separate תרומה for each type of produce, and the משנה says that if someone gives from one type for another, it does not count. So here a forbidden act does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about separating from one type of produce for a different type? The תורה says 'all the best of the oil,' meaning give a best part for this one and a best part for that one. And we learned: One may not separate תרומה from one type for another type, and if he did, it is not תרומה. So it does not work. This is a refutation of אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the attack turns against אביי. Here is a forbidden way of separating תרומה that the משנה says does not work at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires a separate 'best part' for each kind of produce, so giving one type for another is forbidden. The משנה rules that such תרומה is not valid. That goes against אביי's rule that a forbidden act still works.

keyTerms.meaning: From one type of produce for a different type
Here: the best part (not animal fat)
So we see, it follows
It does not work, it has no effect

steps.confusionAlert: Here חֵלֶב means 'the best part' of the produce, not the forbidden animal fat.

phrases.english: But what about separating from one type for a type that is not its own,
as the Merciful One said: "All the best of the oil,"
meaning to give a best part for this one and a best part for that one,

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין מִמִּין עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ,
phrases.english: and we learned in a mishnah: One may not separate terumah from one type for a different type,
and if he did separate,
his terumah is not terumah.
So we see that the forbidden act does not work,
a refutation of Abaye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending both sides on the bad-produce case, the גמרא brings a new case, this time against אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that a forbidden act still works
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק forbids giving from one type for another, and the משנה says such תרומה is not valid. So here a forbidden act does not work.

steps.title: אביי answers from the extra word ראשית
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that this case is special. The פסוק adds the word 'ראשיתם', which teaches again that each type needs its own first part. That extra teaching shows the act does not work here. רבי אילעא also points to this word.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי can answer: That case is different, because the verse says 'their first part,' meaning a first part for this one and a first part for that one. And רבי אילעא also said: 'first part.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself. He says the different-type case is an exception, because the תורה repeats the rule with an extra word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already taught with 'חלב' that each type needs its own portion, and then it repeats the rule with 'ראשיתם'. The extra repetition shows that here the תורה wants the act not to work at all. Without it, אביי's rule would apply and the תרומה would count. רבי אילעא also points to the word ראשית for this case.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part, the portion given as תרומה
The פסוק, the verse

steps.whatToRemember: Each side keeps its general rule and treats the other side's case as an exception taught by a פסוק. For רבא, bad-for-good תרומה works only because of 'you shall bear no sin.' For אביי, different-type תרומה fails only because of the extra word 'ראשיתם'.

phrases.english: Abaye could say to you:
It is different there,
since the verse says "their first part"
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before, במדבר יח:יב. It says the rule a second time.

phrases.english: meaning a first part for this one and a first part for that one.
And Rabbi Ile'a also said: "first part."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תיובתא against אביי from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special exception from an extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The different-type case seemed to prove that forbidden acts do not work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only this case fails, because the extra word 'ראשיתם' teaches it. The general rule that forbidden acts work still stands for אביי.

steps.title: What the word ראשית teaches according to רבא
steps.stepSummary: For רבא, 'ראשית' teaches that even wine and grain, which share one 'חלב', may not be given one for the other. Someone who does so gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבא, what does 'ראשית' teach? If the תורה had not said 'ראשית', I would have thought that only wine and oil, which each get their own word 'חלב' (best), may not be given as תרומה one for the other. But wine and grain, or one grain for another grain, share only one 'חלב'. So if someone gave from one for the other, I would think he does not get מלקות. So the תורה wrote 'ראשית' to teach that he must give the best from this one and the best from that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the extra word 'ראשית' teaches for רבא, and answers that it adds a real איסור (with מלקות) for wine and grain too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי used 'ראשית' to show that the forbidden act does not work. רבא does not need that, because for him a forbidden act never works anyway. So for רבא the word does a different job: it makes the איסור full-strength for wine and grain, which share one 'חלב' in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The first or best part; the extra word in the פסוק about תרומה
Wine (new wine)
Olive oil
Grain
Here it means 'the best part', not animal fat
He gets מלקות (lashes)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חלב' does not mean forbidden fat or milk. In this פסוק it means 'the best part' of the produce.

phrases.english: And according to Rava?
phrases.notes: The question is left unsaid: for רבא, what does the word 'ראשית' come to teach?

phrases.english: If the Merciful One had not said 'the first part',
I would have said: wine and oil,
about which 'best' and 'best' is written,
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:12: 'כל חלב יצהר וכל חלב תירוש ודגן'. Oil gets its own 'חלב', while wine and grain share one.

phrases.english: that one may not give תרומה from this for that.
But wine and grain, or grain and grain,
about which only one 'best' is written,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תָרֵים מֵהַאי אַהַאי — לָא לָקֵי.
phrases.english: when one gives תרומה from this for that, he is not lashed.
So the Merciful One wrote 'the first part',
to give the best for this one and the best for that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי used 'ראשיתם' in step 12, the גמרא asks what that word does for רבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'ראשית' teaches according to רבא, who does not need it to show the act fails.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It extends the full איסור, with מלקות, to wine and grain, which share one 'חלב'.

steps.title: A second version of what ראשית teaches for רבא
steps.stepSummary: Another version: without 'ראשית', one would even be allowed to give wine for grain from the start. The word creates the איסור itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: wine and grain share only one 'חלב', so without this word one could give תרומה from one for the other. So the תורה wrote 'ראשית'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way of saying the answer for רבא, with a stronger claim about what we would have thought without the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, without 'ראשית' it would still be wrong to give wine for grain, just without מלקות. In this version it would be fully allowed. So here 'ראשית' creates the איסור itself, not just the punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same discussion
He may give תרומה from this type for that type

phrases.english: Another version:

phrases.aramaic: הָא תִּירוֹשׁ וְדָגָן, דְּחַד ״חֵלֶב״ כְּתִיב בְּהוּ —
phrases.english: But wine and grain, about which only one 'best' is written,
one may give תרומה from this for that.
So the Merciful One wrote 'the first part'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the answer in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Same question as step 13: what 'ראשית' teaches for רבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It creates the איסור itself for wine and grain, which would otherwise be allowed.

steps.title: Challenge to אביי from dedicated property that may not be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The תורה forbids redeeming חרמים, and the משנה says חרמי כהנים are not redeemed but given to the כהן. This shows the forbidden act does not work, which is a תיובתא against אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at חרמים: the תורה says 'it shall not be sold and shall not be redeemed', and we learned in a משנה: 'חרמי כהנים are not redeemed; rather, they are given to the כהן.' So we see that redeeming does not work. This is a refutation of אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case against אביי, where the תורה forbids an act and the act also fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי says a forbidden act still works. But by חרמים, the תורה forbids redeeming, and the משנה says the item must go to the כהן. That shows redeeming does not take effect, so here a forbidden act does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Property someone dedicates as a חרם
חרמים that go to the כהנים
Redeem (buy back for money)
So we see
It does not work
A strong refutation

phrases.english: But there are dedicated items,
about which the Merciful One said: 'It shall not be sold and shall not be redeemed',

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: חֶרְמֵי כֹהֲנִים אֵין פּוֹדִין אוֹתָם,
phrases.english: and we learned: items dedicated to the priests are not redeemed,
rather, they are given to the priest.
So we see it does not work,
a refutation of Abaye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי answered the challenge from separate types of produce, the גמרא brings another case against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that a forbidden act still takes effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה forbids redeeming חרמים, and the משנה requires giving them to the כהן, showing that the redemption does not take effect.

steps.title: אביי's answer: the verse says חרמים stay as they are
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that חרמים are different, because the פסוק says 'קדש קדשים הוא', which teaches that a חרם must stay in its current state and cannot be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי can tell you: it is different there, because the תורה says 'it is most holy', which means it must stay as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי against the challenge from חרמים. It says that case is special because of a specific פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said that redeeming a חרם does not work, so a forbidden act does not work. אביי answers that the words 'קדש קדשים הוא' teach that a חרם must stay as it is. So it is this פסוק, and not a general rule about forbidden acts, that blocks the redemption. In other cases, the general rule still holds: a forbidden act does work.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; that case is special
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
It is most holy, a phrase from the פסוק about חרמים
It shall stay in its current state
Property dedicated through a vow of dedication

steps.whatToRemember: אביי keeps his rule: a forbidden act still works. The cases where it does not work, like separate תרומה for each type and חרמים, are special because a פסוק adds an extra teaching.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same pattern as the answer about 'ראשיתם' in step 12. Each time, אביי explains the exception through an extra word or phrase in the פסוק.

phrases.english: He could say to you:
phrases.notes: אביי could answer the challenge from חרמים in step 15 like this.

phrases.english: It is different there,
as the Merciful One states: "It is most holy"
it shall be as it is.
phrases.notes: The word 'הוא' (it is) teaches that the חרם stays the way it is, so redeeming it cannot change it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from חרמי כהנים raised in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the פסוק makes חרמים a special exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since redeeming חרמים does not work, it seemed that forbidden acts in general do not work, against אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The failure of redemption comes from 'קדש קדשים הוא', which means a חרם stays as it is. It does not come from a general rule, so אביי's principle stands.
